newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kim Jong-il marks anniverary as military chief.
newsitem.headline: Kim Jong-il marks anniverary as military chief.

text.p: North Koreans have celebrated the fifth anniversary of their leader Kim Jong-il's elevation to the chief of the communist state's armed forces, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said on Thursday.
Kim took over from his father as Supreme Commander of North Korea's 1.1-million-strong military five years ago.
In the North Korean capital of Pyongyang, senior government and party officials took part in a national symposium and heaped praise on Kim.

"With the great comrade Kim Jong-il as the Supreme Commander, the Korean People and People's Army have turned the country and the nation into a strong nation and a powerful socialist state with self-reliant defence," officials told the symposium.
"General Kim Jong-il has brought up the People's Army into human bombs to defend the headquarters of the revolution," they added, according to KCNA monitored in Tokyo.
The 54-year-old Kim has yet to be formally confirmed in the two key posts his late father Kim Il-sung held -- general secretary of the ruling Workers' Party and state president.
Korea watchers in Tokyo and Seoul believe that Kim Jong-il will formally take up the posts in mid-1997.
